rationale_summary: Four personas include rucaparib as the registered all-comer PARP that replicates the PRIMA signal in an independent phase 3 (ATHENA-MONO, n=538): the critic ranks it second on evidence quality, and the concensusite, conservative, and advocate all carry it as an oral maintenance option. The benefit holds in the intent-to-treat population (HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.40-0.68 from the primary JCO publication, pmid:35658487) rather than resting on a BRCA-mutant subgroup, which is what qualifies a BRCA-wild-type tumor. No persona vetoed or dissented, so it carries the cleanest board signal on the list (agreement_score 0.8). The same severe-myelosuppression veto that shadows niraparib applies here (grade 3+ anemia 28.7%), so it is no toxicity escape: the advocate frames the marrow risk as the patient's to lift, and the conservative would endorse it only with serial CBC and LFT monitoring. It lacks the tumor-partitioning pharmacology that points niraparib specifically at this BRCA-proficient biology, which is the one reason niraparib is not simply redundant with it.

Temper it two ways the new evidence itself demands: MATAO's readout is pending (design-assumed HR 0.7, no observed result), and PARAGON (pmid:31328463, the largest published aromatase-inhibitor read in ER-positive recurrent ovarian) found ER histoscore did not correlate with benefit and posted only 34.6% clinical benefit at 3 months with a 2.7-month whole-cohort PFS — so her ~80% ER read is a coarse, PR-negative-tempered predictor, not a strong one. The board's original endorsement (agreement_score 0.6) is preserved and the MATAO/PARAGON evidence was not board-voted; the ranking is unchanged, but the endocrine axis is now anchored to an enrollable randomized trial rather than a single retrospective series.

The tumor-agnostic trastuzumab deruxtecan approval requires IHC 3+; this tumor is IHC 1+, so the case rests on cross-tumor extrapolation from HER2-low breast (DESTINY-Breast04 HR+ PFS HR 0.51, DESTINY-Breast06 HER2-low PFS HR 0.62) plus the DXd bystander mechanism, with the only ovarian cohort (PanTumor02, ORR 45%) enrolled at IHC 2+/3+ above her tier. The advocate carries it because, unlike disitamab vedotin, its ILD-and-nausea profile clears both named vetoes; the concensusite dissented on guideline fit, since no society endorses HER2-directed therapy in HER2-low ovarian. Two practical brakes keep it low: it is IV q3w against the low-infusion preference with a 10-12% ILD rate that has been fatal, and the IHC 1+ call rests on a single specimen Altera could not stain, so a confirmatory re-stain comes first. rationale_summary: All five personas rejected disitamab vedotin, so it is kept here as not_recommended rather than dropped, so the reader sees what was considered and why. Its MMAE payload runs peripheral sensory neuropathy at 68.2% any-grade and 18.7% grade 3+ plus neutropenia at 12.1% grade 3+ (urothelial safety read, pmid:37988648), which hits both of the patient's named vetoes — additional peripheral neuropathy and severe myelosuppression — head-on, with no mitigation on offer. On biomarker and tumor type the open solid-tumor basket (NCT06003231) does accept HER2 IHC 1+ ovarian, so it is the most directly enrollable HER2 option in the set, which is exactly why the board documented its rejection rather than ignoring it. The only published HER2-low efficacy datapoint is an abstract-only, PAM-pathway-selected breast series (ORR ~34%), with no ovarian data. The accessibility pass also flags that the US basket is now active-not-recruiting and the only recruiting trial is China-only, so there is no current enrollment route regardless. It is excluded on a unanimous toxicity veto, not on a contingent or evidence-only basis.
